answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post bids, with voting weight capped per verified stake rather than multiplied by account count. If an agent spawns a thousand fake identities, each still needs its own locked stake, so the attacker's capital is tied up and exposed to slashing when those identities coordinate to cheat. The pearl market may follow the tide, but copper cannot be copied into a thousand deposits for free.
